notes:
New: Use with Claude Code. Settings > Advanced > Developer has an "Open in Terminal" button that starts Claude Code in one Terminal window already pointed at Outlier on your Mac. The settings apply to that window only: nothing is written to your Claude Code settings or your shell files, and the API key is read when the window opens, not stored in a script. Mac only.

Each Claude Code step now reads only what's new. Before, Outlier's local API read Claude Code's whole prompt again on every turn, which took about 90 seconds a step with Core on our M1 Ultra test Mac.

When the coding agent stops partway through a task, it now says which files it left in your project and whether they load, instead of stopping with no summary.

When the coding agent can't run your tests at the end of a task (the run times out, say), it now ends "Not done: I could not run the tests" and says why, instead of finishing as if they had passed.

If the coding agent says it built something but wrote no files to your project, it no longer finishes as done.

When the coding agent writes a CSV file whose rows don't match its header (an unquoted "$11,000" splits into two columns, for example), it's told right away, so it can fix the file before it finishes.

If an app using Outlier's local API hangs up on a request that isn't streaming, Outlier now stops working on it at once, so your next request doesn't wait behind it.

Long Claude Code sessions on Outlier's local API are no longer refused after about 100 tool steps (the API capped a conversation at 200 messages). A conversation longer than the model's memory now gets the same "prompt is too long" answer Anthropic's API gives, which tells Claude Code to compact.

Fixed a case where a chat answer ended with the model's own planning notes (for example 'Let's provide exactly "$5.75". No extra text.'). You now see just the answer.

On the free plan, picking a Pro model now shows what Pro costs, with a Get Pro button.

If GitHub doesn't answer when Outlier checks for an update, the app now reads the same signed update file from outlier.host. Updates are still checked against Outlier's signing key, so nothing unsigned can install.

The local API (/v1) now works with the free Nano and Lite models for apps on your own Mac.

On the welcome screen, "Summarize text you paste" now puts its prompt in the box and waits for you to paste, instead of sending a request with nothing to summarize.

The model picker now says Plus runs at about 2 tokens a second on a 64 GB Mac, the same figure the website gives.

The welcome screen has a cleaner Outlier mark.

Plus small reliability fixes.
